CVE-2026-131239.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Updates data. If another user who can access the System Update Status report selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Update Status report does not validate destination, signature, and vendor-product values before inserting them into drilldown searches.

CVE-2026-132128.title: @fastify/middie vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via Unicode case folding
CVE-2026-132128.description: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7,…

CVE-2026-99698.title: mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address
CVE-2026-99698.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved at a fixed address

CMA areas allocated from memblock have their memory accepted by
memblock_alloc_range_nid(), but areas reserved at a fixed address with
memblock_reserve() are not.

If a fixed CMA area is requested by the cma=<size>@<base> command line
parameter, it may be in regular RAM and on TDX and SEV-SNP guests it
must be accepted.

Accept the memory of fixed CMA areas as well, so that all CMA areas are
accepted regardless of how they were reserved.

CVE-2026-99759.title: batman-adv: tt: don't drop local events queued during TVLV update
CVE-2026-99759.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: don't drop local events queued during TVLV update

batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update() read the number of local changes without
holding changes_list_lock. batadv_tt_local_event() is not serialized by
the commit_lock and can queue new events before the changes_list is
flushed:

CPU0 CPU1
batadv_tt_tvlv_container_update()
num = ...local_changes;
batadv_tt_local_event()
list_add_tail(...);
...local_changes++;
spin_lock_bh(&...changes_list_lock);
/* only num events copied but all freed */

The additional events were freed without ever being sent. Other nodes will
only notice this via a CRC mismatch and must request the full table.

The number of changes and the changes_list must therefore be taken
atomically. Events queued afterwards then stay in the tt.changes_list for
the next TT round.

The changes can no longer be kept for the next round when the TVLV buffer
allocation fails. But they would be sent…
